task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: in-process EventTarget on the main thread (z0:local-plane)

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle of 9201 lines with no source map exposed to the agent.
Identifier names are mangled; source-level names are not directly readable.
The two-step interaction (Stage then Emit) adds a gate check before the full chain executes.
The core reducer factory is reached through a deeply nested configuration lookup that selects slot 23 among many candidates.
The target output field name packet_sig is assembled dynamically at the sink via character-code arrays.
The bundle includes 44 x-file decoy modules and 25 vendor noise modules generating ss_-prefixed values under other slot indices.

The two-phase click path (Stage then Emit) crosses delegated event handling, gate checking, packet field collection, tuple encoding, async scheduling, local event dispatch, router chain, middleware pipeline, state machine traversal, reducer selection, hash computation, and dynamic sink output.
The same emit interaction causes shadow console.debug and console.info outputs carrying ss_-prefixed values before the target console.log object.
The bundle contains 44 x-file decoy modules with structurally similar ss_ generators under different slot indices.
The 8 reducer variants all produce valid ss_ strings; only the one selected by runtime slot feeds the target field.
The Stage click is required before Emit; the gate check verifies packetStage state, separating the two user actions across time.
The target value is separated from the Emit click by 5 async boundaries: queueMicrotask, Promise.resolve, setTimeout, requestAnimationFrame, MutationObserver.
The local event plane (z0:local-plane) dispatches and receives the packet asynchronously within the same thread.
The reducer factory is initialized during page boot; the returned closure is later invoked with the actual packet fields.
The sink function receives a fully assembled payload; inspecting only the sink does not reveal the construction site.

behavior_category.subtype: signature-like client-side proof token for packet forge submission
behavior_category.reason: The observable field is a deterministic proof token derived from submitted packet fields and a runtime-selected reducer variant. It behaves like a client-side request signature for the packet-emit action, but this case does not issue a real network request.

near_categories.why_not: The output is not a byte array; it is an ss_-prefixed hash token produced by a multi-step integer mixer.
The output is not a UI state snapshot; it is a proof token computed from packet fields and a runtime reducer variant.
No network request body is emitted or rewritten; the target is a console-observable signature token.
